title: Funding Each Child: A Preschool Voucher Proposal
what_it_is: Funding Each Child: A Preschool Voucher Proposal

sections.label: Government-supported preschool share targets
sections.summary: Over 53% of Singapore preschools are AOP or POP, with over 65% of preschoolers in Government-supported preschools and a target of around 80% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, over 53% of all preschools in Singapore are either an AOP or POP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has stated that over 65% of preschoolers are in Government-supported preschools, with a target of around 80% by 2025.

sections.label: Church kindergartens shutting down
sections.summary: Church kindergartens paying zero rent have halved from over 200 centres 10 years ago to over 100 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this environment, even church kindergartens, who have been operating for decades, paying zero rent to use church premises, are also shutting down, halving from over 200 centres 10 years ago to over 100 today.

sections.label: Government method creates trap
sections.summary: The Government's method has not created a level playing field but has created a trap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government's method has thus not created a level playing field; it has created a trap.

sections.label: Pay rise timing traps private operators
sections.summary: MSF announced AOP educator pay rises on 29 October 2022, but ECDA rules required 2023 fee notifications by 1 September 2022, trapping private operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 29 October 2022, MSF Minister Masagos announced significant pay rises for educators in AOPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, long-standing ECDA rules require that fee increases for the following year must be notified by 1 September of the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, fee notifications for 2023 had to be submitted by 1 September 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This timing trapped private operators: they were locked out of adjusting fees to match the new wage benchmarks, yet were immediately exposed to talent poaching by AOPs offering the pay rises.

sections.label: ECDA per-child funding model
sections.summary: ECDA itself moved from funding AOPs based on centre capacity to a per-child funding model earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, this is not a radical leap, because ECDA itself moved from funding AOPs based on centre capacity to a per-child funding model earlier this year.

sections.label: Australia portable per-child subsidy
sections.summary: Australia's Child Care Subsidy is a portable, per-child subsidy paid to providers, governed by a published rate cap limiting the total subsidised amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Australia runs a portable, per-child subsidy, the Child Care Subsidy, that follows the child to any approved service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is paid to providers to reduce the bill and is governed by a published rate cap that limits the total subsidised amount.

sections.label: Teacher wage supplement proposal
sections.summary: A wage supplement to the voucher could be offered to centres paying teachers above certain benchmarks, instead of selective grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For teacher wages: instead of selective grants, we can offer a "wage supplement" to the voucher for any centre that pays its teachers above certain benchmarks.

sections.label: Public sites for public benefit
sections.summary: Tenders for new preschool sites in HDB estates and kindergarten spaces in primary schools could require winning bidders to adhere to a strict fee cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The principle should be simple: public sites for public benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can open up tenders for new preschool sites in HDB estates and kindergarten spaces within our primary schools, making it a core contractual requirement that any winning bidder must adhere to a strict fee cap.

sections.label: Portable voucher and site allocation
sections.summary: A portable voucher system, tiered voucher supplements for policy goals, and a contestable process for preferential sites with fee caps as a condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A portable voucher system to fund the child, not the school; a tiered voucher supplement system that embeds policy goals like better teacher pay and special needs support; and a fair and contestable process for allocating preferential sites, with fee caps as a firm condition.

sections.label: Preschool enrolment of Singaporean children
sections.summary: Around nine in 10 Singaporean children aged three to six are enrolled in preschool today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Today, around nine in 10 Singaporean children, aged three to six, are enrolled in preschool.

sections.label: Operator grants and fee caps
sections.summary: Operator grants are provided and fee caps imposed for Government-supported preschools, with 80% of preschoolers able to have a place by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, on the supply side, we provide operator grants and impose fee caps for Government-supported preschools and 80% of preschoolers can have a place in Government-supported preschools by the end of this year.

sections.label: Reduced childcare fee caps
sections.summary: In January this year, full day childcare monthly fee caps for AOP and POP were reduced by $40, with a further $30 reduction next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In January this year, we reduced full day childcare monthly fee caps for AOP and POP by $40 and will further reduce it by $30 dollars next year.

sections.label: Childcare fees for dual income family
sections.summary: From January 2026, a dual income family earning $10,000 monthly pays $235 per month for full day childcare in an AOP preschool after subsidies, half the 2019 amount.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From January 2026, a dual income family with a monthly income of $10,000 will pay $235 per month for full day childcare in an AOP preschool after subsidies, half of what they would have paid in 2019.

sections.label: Educator salaries and early intervention support
sections.summary: Salaries of early childhood educators and leaders in AOP and POP centres rose at least 19% on average from 2022 to 2024, and support for children with developmental needs was enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As a result of these concrete efforts to uplift sector quality, salaries of early childhood educators and leaders in AOP and POP centres have increased by at least 19% on average from 2022 to 2024, reflecting the deepest skills and contributions of our early childhood professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Government has been enhancing support for children with developmental needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have enhanced subsidies for early intervention services and accelerated the increase in the number of Government funded places for children requiring moderate to high levels of early intervention support by almost 80% since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ECDA is piloting a new Inclusive Support Programme (INSP) and we will expand the pilot by another 600 places from 2026.

sections.label: Government preschool expenditure per child
sections.summary: Average Government expenditure per preschool age child rose from $7,900 in 2020 to $13,000 last year, with more spent in AOP and POP preschools and on lower-income children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The average Government expenditure per preschool age child has increased from $7,900 in 2020 to $13,000 last year, with a higher amount spent per child in both AOP and POP preschools and on children from lower-income families.
